title: A characteristic obstruction in higher Koszul homology

native.rights: Native record CC BY 4.0. No separate license terms found in the support archive.

initial.phase: root controlling TeX assessment; independent reviewer already separately sealed before priorities and primary source bodies
initial.claims: For free algebra on finite many letters, every positive-weight orbit O with size d gives one-dimensional higher Koszul homology in each of degrees 0 and 1 exactly when characteristic divides d; otherwise zero. Degree≥2 no groups; constant weight degree0 is ground field. Two letters and word x^(p-1)y give exact counterexample to unrestricted characteristic.
initial.initial: R=0 leaves W0/W1. In positive weight n concatenation identifies degree 1 and 0 chains with the rotation module. Differential 1-ρ and Euler cap map ρ-invariants to coinvariants by multiplication by orbit size. The unique y gives p distinct rotations with nonzero combination in kernel and no incoming boundary; char2 and singleton x^p explicitly controlled. Inverse direction cyclic norm computes n/d; orbit size and weight must not conflate.
initial.questions: Check exact source formulation, BLS all-characteristic definition and cap sign, Loday–Quillen and Goodwillie primary formula assumptions, and whether related notes already explicitly include this known mechanism.

math: The free tensor algebra is Koszul via its length-one linear resolution. With coefficients in itself only degrees 0/1 remain, in fixed weight n giving the rotation difference 1-rho. Left Euler cap becomes the map from invariants to coinvariants, multiplying each orbit component by its number of distinct rotations. Thus in positive characteristic p, and only if p divides the orbit size, each component survives in both higher degrees 0 and 1. The weight-zero single k and absent higher degrees match. The primitive orbit of x^(p−1)y gives a p-dimensional regular cyclic module, a nonzero invariant sum and a zero image modulo coinvariants. Repeated x^p is a singleton. Connes B acts in the opposite direction by the norm scalar n/d, not the Euler scalar d.

adversarial.name: even_markov_adversarial_sol
adversarial.findings: Independently proved bimodule resolution by the path of cuts, and primitive p-orbit as k[u]/u^p. Euler cap is the zero socle-to-top map. Checked BLS definitions and scope, full OWR contribution, LQ and Goodwillie. No archived opinions consulted.

Later related counterexamples use square-zero algebras, a signed rotation and surviving groups in other degrees. Same general obstruction question, distinct class of algebra.
scope: Counterexample to the unrestricted-field forward implication, not the characteristic-zero theorem or converse. Classical formulas and operator receive credit; priority, current global openness and historical intention are not established.

follow_up.formulation: For a connected quadratic algebra over a characteristic-zero field, does HK_hi_0(A) ≅ k and HK_hi_i(A)=0 for every i>0 imply A is Koszul?
follow_up.impact: A proof would make higher Koszul acyclicity a recognition condition for Koszulness in characteristic zero; a counterexample would identify a separate failure of that proposed characterization.
follow_up.credit: Characteristic-zero direction of Berger–Lambre–Solotar Conjecture 6.5. The positive-characteristic paper and inspected square-zero note do not resolve it. State it as a research question examined here without claiming novelty or worldwide openness.
